summary: Splunk HEC audit export intermittently failing with 401/403 after token rotation (auth_error)
description:
Customer reports Splunk HEC destination started failing intermittently with 401/403 shortly after rotating their Splunk HEC token. Some events are still arriving, but exporter health in Console flips between Healthy and Degraded.

Issue summary
- Splunk audit export intermittently fails with 401/403 after token rotation
- Destination health shows: auth_error / http_status=403 (occasionally 401)
- Customer expectation: token rotation should be a clean cutover after updating credentials in Redwood

Impact
- Partial loss of audit events in customer SIEM during failure windows (customer monitoring + compliance correlation affected)
- Export queue backlog grows during auth failures, then drains when auth succeeds

Customer details
- Company: Northbridge Financial
- Sink: Splunk HEC (customer-managed Splunk Cloud)
- Export type: Audit events v1

Timeline (customer)
- Rotated Splunk HEC token ~2025-02-10 16:20 ET
- Noticed missing events ~17:00 ET; console destination status showed intermittent auth failures

Environment
- Redwood Hosted (enterprise)
- Region: us-east

Steps to reproduce / observed behavior
1) Customer rotates Splunk HEC token (creates new token, disables old token within minutes).
2) Customer updates Redwood destination credential in Console (Security → Audit Export → Destination → Edit token) and clicks Save.
3) Customer uses “Send test event” → sometimes succeeds, sometimes returns 403.
4) Export health alternates between:
   - Healthy (events delivered)
   - Degraded: auth_error (403 Invalid token)

What we checked (initial)
- Confirmed destination URL and index are unchanged.
- Confirmed failures are 401/403 responses (not TLS/network).
- Confirmed failures correlate with connector log lines: "splunk_hec_response status=403 body=Invalid token".

Hypothesis
- Worker/connector not consistently reloading the updated token from secrets store after credential update (cached token across workers / instances).
- During rollout / autoscaling, some workers still using old token while others use new token → intermittent success depending on which worker picks up the batch.

Requested from customer
- Exact time old token was disabled
- Whether both tokens could be kept valid in parallel for 30–60 minutes
- Sample HEC error response body (redacted) and HEC endpoint hostname

Workaround attempted
- Pause destination for 2 minutes, then Resume (forces connector refresh on resume path).
- Re-run test event delivery after resume.

Current status
- Ongoing investigation with Security Eng (SIEM export) and Platform Control Plane on secret propagation / reload behavior across workers.
comments: 2025-02-10 09:18 PT — Fatima Noor (Support): Acknowledged receipt. Asked customer for exact rotation timestamps and whether the previous token was disabled immediately. Shared guidance: for at-least-once pipelines, recommend keeping old token active during cutover to avoid delivery gaps while exporters refresh credentials. Linked Splunk HEC setup guide section “Token rotation / validation”.

2025-02-10 10:02 PT — Customer (Northbridge Financial): Old token was disabled ~5 minutes after new token created. They updated Redwood destination token right away. Seeing 403 “Invalid token” intermittently; some events continue to arrive. They can re-enable the old token temporarily if needed but prefer not to.

2025-02-10 10:27 PT — Kevin Osei (Security Eng): Looked at exporter metrics for tenant. Error spikes show multiple distinct worker instances returning 403 while others succeed. This pattern is consistent with token mismatch across a pool rather than Splunk intermittently rejecting. Suspect credential refresh isn’t happening on all workers (cache TTL too long or refresh path not triggered by destination update).

2025-02-10 11:05 PT — Kevin Osei (Security Eng): Recommended workaround: Pause destination, wait for status to go Paused, then Resume and immediately “Send test event”. This should force refresh on all active workers as they re-acquire destination config. Also asked customer to keep both tokens valid for 30 minutes if possible to avoid gaps while backlog drains.

2025-02-10 11:42 PT — Fatima Noor (Support): Customer applied Pause/Resume. Test event succeeded 3/3 times. Destination remained Healthy for ~20 minutes, then flipped back to Degraded with 403 again. Customer confirmed autoscaling occurred during that window (saw new exporter pods).

2025-02-10 12:18 PT — Kevin Osei (Security Eng): Confirmed: new worker instances appear to start with old credential snapshot for this destination (likely from cached config read) until a periodic refresh. Intermittency explained by mixed pool. Action: coordinate with Platform team to force immediate invalidation/refresh on destination credential update and on startup. In the meantime, operational workaround is to re-save destination credentials (Edit → Save) after scale events, or temporarily disable old token only after confirming all workers refreshed.

2025-02-11 08:36 PT — Benji Okafor (Platform): Found that destination credential update triggers control-plane write, but worker-side config watcher only polls on a 10-minute interval; additionally, Splunk connector caches auth header per client instance. Proposed immediate fix: on 401/403, force client rebuild + re-fetch secret, then retry with backoff. Longer-term: push-based invalidation event to workers.

2025-02-11 10:11 PT — Fatima Noor (Support): Shared interim rotation guidance with customer: (1) Create new HEC token, keep old token enabled, (2) Update Redwood destination token and click Save, (3) Use “Send test event” and verify health stays Healthy for 10–15 minutes, (4) Only then disable old token. Customer agreed and re-enabled old token to stabilize while we implement fix.

2025-02-12 14:02 PT — Kevin Osei (Security Eng): Hotfix deployed to us-east exporter fleet: on Splunk HEC 401/403, rebuild client and reload credential; if still failing, mark destination Degraded with explicit auth_error and suppress retry storm. After deploy, tenant error rate dropped to baseline and backlog drained. Customer can now disable old token safely after verification.

2025-02-13 09:25 PT — Fatima Noor (Support): Customer confirmed: rotated token again following guidance; no intermittent 401/403 observed. Destination Healthy and Splunk search shows continuous events across cutover. Closing ticket; keeping internal follow-up to reduce polling interval / add push invalidation.
resolution: Resolved by (1) providing customer cutover guidance to keep both Splunk HEC tokens valid during rotation until exporter refresh completes, and (2) deploying a hotfix to the Splunk connector/exporter behavior in us-east: on 401/403 responses, the connector forces credential reload and client rebuild before retrying, preventing mixed-token intermittency across autoscaled workers. Customer validated successful rotation with continuous event delivery and no further auth_error states.
follow_up_actions: Create engineering task to reduce worker config polling interval and/or implement push-based invalidation on destination credential changes.
Update Splunk HEC setup guide with explicit token-rotation steps and recommended overlap window (30–60 min) for enterprise customers.
Add alerting to detect mixed auth errors across worker pool for a single destination (indicator of stale credential cache).
